chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: First sight of Billie Holiday at the Mad House
summary: Danny and Smitty saw a young Billie Holiday demanding her pay at the Mad House and later waiting tables across the street.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Well, I was out at the Nest Club. And upstairs over the Nest Club was the Mad House. And Roscoe, who was a hustler, a young, handsome hustler, he owned this joint. That was the first time I saw Billie Holiday. We went in there, me and Smitty, and we sat down. A girl come out the back, this fine-looking, brownskin girl, very defiant, and she starts bitchin' with some guys to give her some money. It seemed like she had served some love or something in there... You know, we don't want to mention the ..(?).., we

don't want to talk about people. But she wanted her money. And they were trying to (?) her because she's a woman. And she said she wouldn't leave there until they gave her all her money. And they gave her her money, and as she passed she said some cuss-words and she went out.

Well, the door was open. I seen she went across the street to... You had to look at her twice because she was such a fine young girl, and to see that... You know, to hear her involved in something like that... So later on I go across to Pa and Jerry's, because they was tellin' me about the Lion, and I went over there and I seen her in there. And she was waiting tables, and later on she sang. So there was... Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy Dorsey, Bert Lom, Paul Whiteman, everybody, all the White musicians used to go to Pa and Jerry's in the morning to get that chicken that they served, just like at Tillie's next door.
